# 172 · A retry route that dead-letters a delivery out of attempts sends the dead letter twice

[← All examples](../README.md)

| Verdict | Categories | Severity if shipped | Change | Verified unit | Approach |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **✗ Violation: counterexample found** | functional | medium | refactor, behaviour change not intended | [`DeliveryFailures#failed`](../../examples/apps/deliveries/src/main/java/net/terminalvalue/deliveries/DeliveryFailures.java) | [B9: Regression verification](../../lib/README.md) |

> The same refactor of the failure route and its retry policy, with the case of a delivery out of attempts handled first: it is dead-lettered whatever the receiver answered, and the route then goes on to ask the policy, which refuses, and dead-letters it again. The answer is the same and every test passes; the effect check finds the duplicate send, in exact order, and replays it on a JVM.

Tags: [messaging](../README.md#tag-messaging), [resilience](../README.md#tag-resilience), [spring-boot](../README.md#tag-spring-boot), [duplicate-delivery](../README.md#tag-duplicate-delivery), [effect-trace](../README.md#tag-effect-trace), [own-checker](../README.md#tag-own-checker)

## The change

Crosscut's `RetryPolicy.shouldRetry` is rewritten as one expression over two named helpers, `notProcessed` (429, 503) and `mayHaveRun` (408, and a server error other than 501, written `status / 100 == 5`), and the route `POST /deliveries/failures` is reorganised around the policy's answer, each send moved into a private method of its own (`scheduleRetry`, `deadLetter`). On the way, the case of a delivery out of attempts is made explicit at the top of the route: it is dead-lettered whatever the receiver answered. The branch has no `return`, so the route goes on to the policy, which refuses to retry, and dead-letters it at the end as before.

**Before** ([`DeliveryFailures.java`](../../examples/apps/deliveries/src/main/java/net/terminalvalue/deliveries/DeliveryFailures.java), line 26):

```java

    @PostMapping("/deliveries/failures")
    public int failed(@RequestParam int status, @RequestParam boolean idempotent, @RequestParam int attempts) {
        if (RetryPolicy.shouldRetry(status, idempotent, attempts, MAX_ATTEMPTS)) {
            kafka.send("delivery-retries", new RetryScheduled(status, attempts + 1));
            return 202;
        }
        kafka.send("delivery-dead-letters", new DeadLettered(status, attempts));
        return 200;
    }
}
```

**After:**

```java

    @PostMapping("/deliveries/failures")
    public int failed(@RequestParam int status, @RequestParam boolean idempotent, @RequestParam int attempts) {
        if (attempts >= MAX_ATTEMPTS) {
            deadLetter(status, attempts); // out of attempts, whatever the receiver answered
        }
        if (RetryPolicy.shouldRetry(status, idempotent, attempts, MAX_ATTEMPTS)) {
            scheduleRetry(status, attempts + 1);
            return 202;
        }
        deadLetter(status, attempts);
        return 200;
    }

    private void scheduleRetry(int status, int next) {
        kafka.send("delivery-retries", new RetryScheduled(status, next));
    }

    private void deadLetter(int status, int attempts) {
        kafka.send("delivery-dead-letters", new DeadLettered(status, attempts));
    }
}
```

```diff
--- a/examples/apps/crosscut/src/main/java/net/terminalvalue/crosscut/retry/RetryPolicy.java
+++ b/examples/apps/crosscut/src/main/java/net/terminalvalue/crosscut/retry/RetryPolicy.java
@@ -14,15 +14,16 @@
      * idempotent request only, that it may not have (408, and the 5xx range except 501, which no retry will fix).
      */
     public static boolean shouldRetry(int status, boolean idempotent, int attempt, int maxAttempts) {
-        if (attempt >= maxAttempts) {
-            return false;
-        }
-        if (status == 429 || status == 503) {
-            return true;
-        }
-        if (!idempotent) {
-            return false;
-        }
-        return status == 408 || (status >= 500 && status <= 599 && status != 501);
+        return attempt < maxAttempts && (notProcessed(status) || idempotent && mayHaveRun(status));
+    }
+
+    /** 429 and 503: the server says it did not process the request. */
+    private static boolean notProcessed(int status) {
+        return status == 429 || status == 503;
+    }
+
+    /** 408, and a server error other than 501, which no retry will fix: the request may have run, or not. */
+    private static boolean mayHaveRun(int status) {
+        return status == 408 || status / 100 == 5 && status != 501;
     }
 }
```

## What the verifier found

The two builds disagree on what the entry point does at its boundary. The checker found this request, and the verifier replayed it on the JVM against both builds, under the same recording stubs:

| Request | Before: outcome; attempts | After: outcome; attempts |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /deliveries/failures: status=0, idempotent=false, attempts=5` | `returns 200; KafkaTemplate.send(topic="delivery-dead-letters", data.status=0, data.attempts=5, data.attempt=absent, data.class=net.terminalvalue.deliveries.DeadLettered)` | `returns 200; KafkaTemplate.send(topic="delivery-dead-letters", data.status=0, data.attempts=5, data.attempt=absent, data.class=net.terminalvalue.deliveries.DeadLettered); KafkaTemplate.send(topic="delivery-dead-letters", data.status=0, data.attempts=5, data.attempt=absent, data.class=net.terminalvalue.deliveries.DeadLettered)` |

The domain is `status: int × idempotent: boolean × attempts: int (the request's inputs, the same in both builds)`. An attempt is a modeled call made, with its payload as it was at the call: the replay ran under recording stubs, not against a broker.

## Would the existing tests have caught it?

No: every existing unit test passes (`java -ea net.terminalvalue.deliveries.Tests`, run against the patched code).

## Why it matters

Every delivery that runs out of attempts reaches the dead-letter topic twice. An operator who replays the topic replays the delivery twice, and a receiver that is not idempotent (the reason most deliveries are dead-lettered rather than retried) runs it twice; an alert that counts dead letters counts double. The route's answer is unchanged, and the tests, which look at the answer and the last record sent, pass.

## Why the verdict is right

The trace of attempted sends is compared exactly, in order and in number: one dead letter against the same dead letter twice is a different trace, even with equal payloads. The checker finds a request with the attempts at the maximum, shrinks it, and replays it on a JVM under the recording stubs: the old route attempts one `send`, the new one two identical ones.

## What to do

Return after the dead letter in the new branch, or drop the branch: the policy already refuses a delivery out of attempts, and the end of the route dead-letters it.

## Notes

- Checked by `jvmcontract effects`, which build.py runs as the B9 check of the route app (`run_tool_effects`). Run inline on 2026-11-07 (JDK 25.0.5): refuted. The checker found `status=20, idempotent=true, attempts=20` in its first search stage ([0:20]) and shrank it in 19 interpreter runs to `status=0, idempotent=false, attempts=5`, on which both builds answer 200, the old one attempting one `send` to `delivery-dead-letters` and the new one the same send twice; replayed on the JVM under the recording stubs.
- The trace is compared in exact order and in number, so two equal attempts are not one: the check would not pass a duplicate even if the payloads were all that a consumer looked at.
- The tests pass: `deadLettersADeliveryOutOfAttempts` looks at the last record sent, which is the right dead letter. A test that counted the records sent would catch it.
- The route sends two classes of payload through one `KafkaTemplate.send`, a `RetryScheduled` and a `DeadLettered`, so the recording stub reads each payload path through the class the payload is (`data.attempt` is absent from a dead letter, `data.attempts` from a retry) and snapshots the class itself as `data.class`, so that a retry and a dead letter with equal values are different attempts. Before this example the narrow case refused such a call ("the call sites pass 2 classes of argument, and a stub reads one").
